catalog.name: Moonlit Lake
catalog.description: Open banks around a cold lake. Easy to cross around, hard to own.

catalog.name: Whispering Forest
catalog.description: Dense timber, narrow clearings, and room for the roads to branch again.

catalog.name: Spider Hollow
catalog.description: A web-choked hollow. Every living enemy authored here is a spider.

catalog.name: Cat's Hearths
catalog.description: The cat, its fire, and two hearths gone cold. Wake a branch and carry flame.

catalog.name: Astronaut's Crater
catalog.description: A stranded astronaut and a field of samples. The pickaxe cracks them open.

catalog.name: Businessman's Timber
catalog.description: Dry timber in tidy rows, and a businessman who calls it inventory. Axe included.

catalog.name: Workman's Ford
catalog.description: A workman, his hazard boots, and a glowing pool with something sunk in it.

catalog.name: Artist's Beds
catalog.description: The artist dug her beds already. Seeds are pigment; the meadow is the canvas.

catalog.name: Salesman's Pond
catalog.description: A salesman with one free sample: a bucket, and the pond to fill it in.

catalog.name: Poet's Pines
catalog.description: Living pines crowd the poet's verse. The great axe fells even living wood.

catalog.name: Death's Meadow
catalog.description: Death, off duty, lends the scythe. The tall grass grew too loud; reap it.

catalog.name: Granite Pass
catalog.description: Standing granite no axe answers. Bats nest in the pass, and iron sleeps under the cliffs.

catalog.name: Sunken Graveyard
catalog.description: A paved yard of tombs under dead trees. Three open graves have not finished being graves.

catalog.name: Blooming Grove
catalog.description: Fruit pines and flowering ones over soft dug earth. Nothing here bites; everything grows.

catalog.name: Death's Threshold
catalog.description: A paved ring under old pines, and someone standing in the middle of it. The road ends here — for now.

catalog.name: Cat's Woodpile
catalog.description: A cat, an axe, and a quiet wall of dead wood with iron behind it.

catalog.name: Cat's Kindling
catalog.description: A lit hearth, a stick, and dry brush that only fire will open.

catalog.name: Cat's Quarry
catalog.description: A cat, a pickaxe, a wall of stone and two veins that never run dry.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The dark did not leave us a world. It left us choices.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take the sword. The dead on unfinished roads still carry coin.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Stand on a road seal and press B. Spend what you earn, and decide what exists next.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A hero. How novel. I was napping.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: That branch beside me? Take it. Hold it into my fire and it wakes as a TORCH.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Two hearths in this clearing sit cold. Carry the flame to them.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Light draws a line the dead will not cross. I sleep better behind lines.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My ship is a shell now. What she still needs is IRON — and this crater keeps it locked inside rock.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take the PICKAXE. The veined boulders never run dry: three good swings, one lump of ORE.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ore is not iron yet. Two stones make a FURNACE on that bench, and stone plus ore makes an ALTAR — the slab you hammer on.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Burn dead wood into CHARCOAL in the furnace, smelt it with ore for a SPONGE, then lay the sponge on the altar and strike it three times.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Do it by hand, or build the extractor and the trip hammer and let them work while you walk. Either way, I pay nine coins a bar.

trade.offer: Iron! Nine coins a bar — hull plating is worth every one. How many are you selling?
trade.empty: No iron in that pack. Ore from the veins, charcoal from the burnt scrub, and the furnace does the rest.
trade.thanks: Another plate on the hull. Keep them coming.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Timber. That is the market now.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: This AXE is yours — consider it an advance. It fells DEAD wood in a chop or two.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: My dry ranks stand in rows. Clear them, and the sticks are pure profit.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Sticks build bridges. Bridges open markets. Work hard.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Suit says the pool up north-east glows. Nothing my BOOTS cannot walk.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take them. LAVA BOOTS — lava, embers, and yes, water: you just wade in.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Something metal sank by the little island. Boots on. Go fish it out.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mind this: in deep water your hands stay busy — the boots carry YOU, not cargo.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Zero! Perfect timing. This field is a canvas, and it is BLANK.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take these SEEDS. My pigments. The beds along the south edge are already dug.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Stand before a bed and press A to plant. Water wakes them — rain, or a bucket.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Green is a colour you GROW. Paint me a meadow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Friend! You look thirsty. Or dry. Either way — opportunity.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Free sample: this BUCKET. Fill it in my pond, just west of the fire.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A full bucket waters crops and drowns small fires. Endless uses. Zero coins. Today only.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Tell your friends. If you find any out there.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The pines sing, but they crowd the verse.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: This GREAT AXE fells even LIVING trees — the small axe only knows dead wood.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Open a clearing in my grove. Listen how the song changes where light falls.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Every good line needs its silence. Cut me one.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: You bought your way here, field by field. I watched your furnace smoke cross three of them.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: This is where the road stops. Everything past me is unbuilt — no cards, no coins, no dark to light.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: So: the prologue is over, and you are the one who finished it. Thank you for testing my small world.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Go back and light something. I will wait. Waiting is the one thing I am good at.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. Dead wood. Your sword will not move it — a blade cuts what bleeds.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The AXE is at my feet. Take it, face a dead tree, and press X. Four swings and it comes down.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: A felled tree leaves a STICK behind. Keep every one of them: a stick is a torch that has not met fire yet.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Behind that wall there is iron, and nothing guarding it. Nothing walks in here. Take your time. Mrrow.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. My hearth is lit. Yours is a stick on the ground.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Take the STICK. Face my fire and press X: it wakes as a TORCH. It burns for a while and then it dies — come back and light it again.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Dry brush cannot be chopped. It BURNS. Touch one with the torch and the fire walks to its neighbours on its own.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Burnt brush leaves CHARCOAL on the ground. Bring it to me and I pay in coin — talk to me again when your hands are full.

trade.offer: Charcoal. I will take it off your hands — two coins the lump. How many?
trade.empty: Your hands are empty. Burn some brush and come back.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Mrrow. Stone does not burn and it does not chop. It BREAKS.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The PICKAXE is at my feet. Face a rock, press X, and press it again. The rock opens and leaves a STONE where it stood.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: The boulders with red veins never open. Every three blows they spit out ORE instead — and they never run dry.

lines.speaker: npc
lines.text: Ore is not iron. That is a lesson for a hotter day. Bring the ORE to me and I pay in coin.

trade.offer: Ore. Rust-stained rock. Three coins apiece — how many?
trade.empty: Nothing in your hands. Work a vein and come back.
